name: Reaiah
overview: Reaiah is a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant, a role indicating his involvement in the religious duties associated with the sanctuary. His identification as a Levite aligns him with the priestly tribe chosen to serve God in the tabernacle and later in the temple. This brief mention highlights his participation in the community dedicated to worship and service.
namesAndTitles: The name Reaiah means 'y-h-v-h has seen,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's awareness and involvement. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 2:47, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine observation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Reaiah as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships or genealogical details are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Reaiah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant during the post-exilic period, as noted in Ezra 2:47. His mention underscores the restoration of proper worship and the reestablishment of the Levitical duties after the return from Babylonian captivity. Though briefly noted, his presence affirms the continuity of God's covenant people serving faithfully in the house of the Lord.
